_meta.description: Authoritative source registry for values used by TRIARCHY. This file is intentionally separate from the five locked gameplay contracts so NASA data can be refreshed without changing their schemas.
_meta.policy: A numeric value may be marked verified:true in a gameplay contract only when its source_id, product/version, spatial or table reference, units, and retrieval date are recorded here or in the field source text. Derived gameplay modifiers must remain identified as derived.
_meta.refresh_policy: Check source landing pages before each release and refresh snapshots when a source product version changes. Preserve the prior value and provenance in version control.

sources.title: Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS)
sources.version_or_coverage: NASA reference page updated 2025-04-04: Water Recovery System recovers and recycles about 90 percent of station water
sources.measurement_note: The simulator applies this ISS operational figure as a whole-loop water-recovery proxy. It does not claim that an unbuilt lunar outpost uses the same hardware, recovery streams, or reliability.

sources.title: Moon Fact Sheet
sources.measurement_note: The character controller uses 1.62 m/s² for downward acceleration. Walking speed and jump velocity are gameplay controls, not NASA measurements.

sources.title: LOLA Reduced Data Records and gridded elevation products

sources.measurement_note: Historical source record for the prior south-polar site set. The current coordinates use the global GDR LDEM_4 source record below.

sources.title: LEND Derived Data Records
sources.data_kind: neutron flux and hydrogen-related resource potential
sources.version_or_coverage: PDS LRO LEND archive, Release 67 current at retrieval; LEND_RDR_ALDS_20090915, 2009-09-15 through 2011-12-11, 0.5° × 0.5° south-polar cells
sources.measurement_note: Historical source record for the prior south-polar site set. The cited >88° regional result does not cover any of the current four landing coordinates.

sources.title: Background and Lunar Neutron Populations Detected by LEND and Average Concentration of Near-Surface Hydrogen near the Moon's Poles
sources.version_or_coverage: Livengood et al., Planetary and Space Science 162 (2018); approximately 140 ppmw H above 88° north or south latitude, 0.13 ± 0.02 wt% WEH
sources.measurement_note: Historical source record for the prior south-polar site set. The cited >88° regional result does not cover any of the current four landing coordinates.

sources.title: Cosmic Ray Telescope for the Effects of Radiation data archive and lunar-surface radiation publications
sources.data_kind: lunar-orbit radiation environment and CRaTER-informed lunar-surface context
sources.version_or_coverage: CRaTER measures galactic and solar cosmic radiation behind tissue-equivalent plastic; site-independent baseline uses the separately cited NASA lunar-surface GCR model
sources.measurement_note: CRaTER observations characterize the lunar radiation environment and biological response. They are not a geographic surface-dose raster, so the simulator uses a documented, site-independent NASA lunar-surface GCR baseline before applying its explicit terrain gameplay proxy.

sources.title: NASA Human System Risk Board Review and Risk Mitigation Plan: Risk of Space Radiation Cancer
sources.version_or_coverage: Table 8.4-2, solar-minimum, no-shielding lunar surface: 0.90 mSv/day; BON2020 2009 solar-minimum environment
sources.measurement_note: This is the source of the simulator's 0.90 mSv/sol GCR baseline. It is a site-independent modeled effective dose, not an observed dose at one of the four landing points.

sources.title: LOLA Gridded Data Record global elevation and slope products
sources.product_file: PDS Geosciences Node LDEM_4.IMG / LDEM_4.LBL and LDSM_16.IMG / LDSM_16.LBL
sources.data_kind: Global lunar elevation/shape relative to the 1,737.4 km reference sphere
sources.version_or_coverage: LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0; LDEM_4 (product v3.0, 4 pixels/degree, 7.58084 km/pixel) and LDSM_16 (product v2.0, 16 pixels/degree, 1.89521 km/pixel; 240 m slope baseline); global 0–360° east longitude
sources.measurement_note: Elevation is the LDEM_4 containing-pixel DN × 0.5 m relative to the 1,737.4 km reference sphere. Slope is sampled directly from the LDSM_16 containing pixel and converted by DN × 0.0015 + 45 degrees. The LDSM measurement baseline is 240 m; neither global raster is a local landing-pad survey.
